facts: The Fed lowered its policy rate range to 0 to 0.25 percent in response to the coronavirus shock.
It said the pandemic would weigh on activity in the near term and pose risks to the outlook.
It expected to maintain this range until the economy had weathered recent events; its 2 percent inflation objective was a policy goal, not a known future outcome.

It aimed for inflation moderately above 2 percent for some time after earlier undershooting; this was a policy assessment, not a known future result.

facts: The Fed kept its policy rate range at 0 to 0.25 percent and announced a reduction in the pace of asset purchases.
It said elevated inflation largely reflected factors expected to be transitory, including pandemic supply and demand imbalances.
It expected easing supply constraints to help reduce inflation; this was a policy assessment, not an observed future result.

facts: The Fed raised its policy rate range to 0.75 to 1 percent and anticipated further increases.
It cited pandemic supply and demand imbalances, energy prices, the Ukraine invasion and China lockdowns as inflation pressures.
It expected tighter policy to help inflation return to its longer-run 2 percent objective; this was an expectation, not a known next-year outcome.

facts: The Fed raised its policy rate range to 5 to 5.25 percent.
It said inflation remained elevated and tighter credit conditions were likely to weigh on activity, hiring and inflation, with uncertain effects.
It would assess cumulative tightening and policy lags when judging further firming, and reaffirmed its longer-run 2 percent objective.
